newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Central Bank probes gold trade scam.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Central Bank probes gold trade scam.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank is investigating two employees suspected of demanding unauthorized payments from foreign banks involved in Brazil's gold transactions, a Central Bank official said Wednesday.
"There is still some doubt as to the amounts involved, but it's probably not more than $2 million," Gustavo Franco, the bank's director of international affairs told reporters.

The two employees, one of whom was a gold trader, had been suspended and might face criminal proceedings if an internal Central Bank investigation came up with evidence they demanded and received unauthorized commissions, Franco said.

The Central Bank's policy is not to charge commissions on banks involved in its gold operations. However, a foreign bank complained it had been paying commissions to a financial institution based in Uruguay for its role as a partner to the Central Bank's gold trade, Franco said. He declined to name the bank involved nor its country of origin.
The Central Bank began investigating the two employees two months ago and informed public prosecutors and a federal government accounting agency of its inquiry April 30.
There were also signs that an employee of the foreign bank might also be involved in the scam, Franco said.
